text:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: KV cache size growth on inference-pool-7 (>3x baseline) for model group 'llama-mqa' — latency up, enqueue backlog rising. pagerduty: @oncall-raj paged.

Raj Patel: I'm on it, looking at shard metrics now. seeing continuous-batch queue length spike on shard-7a.

Sasha Li: Confirmed — KV entries growing by prefix length for a subset of requests with long system prompts. 95th latency jumped from 120ms -> 850ms. No OOMs yet but tail CPU on the host is pegged.

Mike Chen: Hypothesis: recent continuous-batching tuning (aggressive prefetch + higher max_batch_tokens) exposed an MQA corner where cache keys weren't deduping for partially-overlapping prefixes. Need immediate mitigation: reduce batch window and disable prefetch on affected runtime.

Raj Patel: Agreed. Mitigation plan: 1) Disable prefetch on pool 7. 2) Drop max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 768. 3) Force fallback to llama-quant-v2 for heavy tails. Doing 1&2 now.

Mike Chen: Patch to runtime config:
```json
{"op":"replace","path":"/pools/7/runtime/prefetch_enabled","value":false}
{"op":"replace","path":"/pools/7/runtime/max_batch_tokens","value":768}
```

deploy-bot: Patch posted to cluster: runtime-configs/pool-7 patched (rolling update) — sha: fe3a2b4. Starting 10% canary -> 100% if green.

Noah Glover: Canary looks good so far on two nodes, KV growth stopped in canary window. I'll promote to full rollout. Also kicking a model-fallback for high-latency routes: route rule -> llama-quant-v2.

Noah Glover: Rollout command: `redwoodctl rollout apply --route heavy-prefix --model llama-quant-v2 --mode immediate` — executed.

Eli (support): Notifying impacted customers: saw ~12 distinct API keys with elevated 5xx/latency over last 7m. Escalated to account owners for proactive comms.

Sasha Li: Quick logs from one affected worker (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-15T14:32:09Z] kv_cache: insert key=prefix:abcd123 len=4096
[2026-03-15T14:32:10Z] batch_worker: queued tokens=1900, batching_window_ms=120
[2026-03-15T14:32:10Z] kv_cache: total_entries=312000 usage=3.8GB
[2026-03-15T14:32:11Z] infer: latency=730ms status=200
```
This matches overlap scenario, MQA tokenization producing long repeated prefixes.

Raj Patel: After rollout complete: all pools report KV growth stabilized, 95p latency back to ~140ms, error rate fell to baseline. Opening handoff for followups and postmortem.

Mike Chen: Short-term postmortem notes: root cause likely interaction of continuous-batching prefetch + MQA prefix fragmentation leading to duplicate KV entries. Next actions: revert the aggressive prefetch change, add a dedupe pass for proximal prefixes in KV layer, add a governor on KV insertion rate per-request.

Eli (support): Customer impact summary to include in incident page: ~12 keys, ~5 customers with visible user impact (page loads slow / transient 5xx), no data exposure, actions taken, ETA for full root-cause fix requested.

Raj Patel: Handoff — I'm off in 20m. Sasha will continue on-call for followups and coordinate postmortem write-up. @Sasha Li please pick up action items. :wave:

Sasha Li: Got it, I'll own the postmortem and schedule a fiber-deep repro run against MQA tokenization. Will also open a short-lived alert to watch KV insertion rate over next 72h.

deploy-bot: Final status: rollout completed at 2162511200, all checks green.

incident-bot: Incident closed for now (mitigated) — trackers: INC-21625, PMT-748.

Raj Patel: Thanks team. Follow-ups: PR for dedupe guard, config rollback for prefetch, customer notes.
